Creates none that were absent (ls -a afterwards shows only what was seeded plus AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/.gitignore/.pact). Skips .clinerules when it is a directory (still 'drwxrwxr-x .clinerules', no error). init --json gained an instruction_files array listing exactly the four managed paths.

The bead worried each target needs a decision because a format with no import mechanism would need the block COPIED, reintroducing drift. That was avoided entirely: every target gets a POINTER, never a copy. GEMINI.md and copilot get prose + '@AGENTS.md' (both expand @-imports); .cursorrules/.windsurfrules get the same prose WITHOUT the @ line, since a dangling @ reads as a broken link. 'grep -c PACT_AGENT GEMINI.md' -> 0: the protocol text exists in exactly one file, so is_current() still has exactly one copy to police.

HALF 2 - doctor reports staleness for each. This is the half that was NOT done when the implementer handed off; fixer wired it. Verified live:

  ✓ other instruction files current: 4 up to date
  $ sed -i 's/Read `AGENTS.md`/Read AGENTS.md maybe/' GEMINI.md   # corrupt inside the markers
  $ pact doctor
  ✗ other instruction files current: missing or stale — run `pact init`: GEMINI.md
  EXIT=1

REGRESSION FOUND BY TWO VERIFIERS AND FIXED, verified by me: the first implementation filtered targets with path.is_file(), which follows symlinks, so 'ln -s AGENTS.md GEMINI.md' made init splice the pointer block through the link and DESTROY the protocol in AGENTS.md, permanently (every subsequent init re-wiped it).   1
  $ pact init --no-commit && pact doctor | grep 'AGENTS.md block'
  ✓ AGENTS.md block current: up to date

ALL THREE CLAUSES VERIFIED BY THE CLOSER against real bd 1.1.2 and real br 0.2.19, in scratch workspaces, with target/debug/pact.

CLAUSE 1 - 'locates br and prefers it over bd when both are present, falling back to bd otherwise'. MET, WITH ONE DELIBERATE NARROWING that is recorded here because the code, not this bead text, is now the truth. Shipped rule: an existing .beads/ store PINS the backend (embeddeddolt/ -> bd, *.db -> br, both -> bd); br is preferred only when there is no store yet. Verified both directions:
  br init workspace:  pact whoami --json -> "bd_binary":"br", "bd_version":"br 0.2.19", "problems":[]
  bd init workspace:  pact whoami --json -> "bd_binary":"bd", "bd_version":"bd version 1.1.2 (20e493e56)"
  this repo (BOTH stores on disk after a stray br init, both binaries on PATH): pact whoami -> bd
Unconditional 'prefer br' would have been a data-loss-shaped bug: the backends do not share a store, so on any machine with both installed every existing bd repo would have opened an empty SQLite database and reported an empty inbox. The bead's wording is the thing that was wrong; nobody should 'fix' the code to match it.

CLAUSE 2 - every flag msg.rs relies on has a br equivalent discovered empirically. Re-run by me against br 0.2.19, not taken on trust:
  br create --type=message --title= --description= --assignee= --actor= --json
    -> {"id":"...","issue_type":"message","assignee":"bravo","created_by":"alpha",...}  WORKS, same argv as bd
  --parent, label add <ids...> <label>  WORKS, byte-identical argv to bd, idempotent -> the read-by-<agent> read-state mechanism needed zero code change
  --no-inherit-labels -> 'error: unexpected argument' — GAP, and correctly handled by omission rather than emulation: a br child is born with no labels, so the bug the flag prevents cannot occur there
  --include-infra     -> 'error: unexpected argument' — GAP, unnecessary: plain br list already returns message beads, and br has the --type filter bd lacks
Two divergences the bead did not anticipate, both handled: br list --json is an envelope {issues,total} not a bare array, and br list omits parent AND has no --parent filter — so on br every listing is list + one show, and thread replies come from the root's parent-child dependents.
